name: ofa-vscode
description: One-click SLURM + ofa connection for VS Code Chat on Kestrel and other HPC systems.

ofa.kestrelHostnamePattern.markdownDescription: Regex used to confirm that a Remote-SSH host is a Kestrel node. If your site uses different hostnames, override this so `OFA: Connect` still recognizes it. Matched against the output of `uname -n` on the remote.

ofa.slurm.account.markdownDescription: Slurm account for the `salloc` request. Empty string = auto-detect via `sacctmgr` (same behaviour as `bin/ofa`).

ofa.slurm.partition.markdownDescription: Slurm partition for the `salloc` request. Empty = inherit from `bin/ofa` (site.toml `[scheduler].partition`, else the Kestrel default `debug`). Set to override per-user.

ofa.slurm.walltime.markdownDescription: Wall time for the `salloc` request (`HH:MM:SS`). Empty = inherit from `bin/ofa` (site.toml `[scheduler].walltime`, else `00:30:00`).

ofa.slurm.gres.markdownDescription: Slurm GRES for the `salloc` request. Empty = inherit from `bin/ofa` (site.toml `[scheduler].gres`, else `gpu:1`). Set to `gpu:h100:1` or similar on sites with typed GPU GRES.

ofa.ofaBinPath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the `ofa` executable. Leave empty to auto-detect (checks `$OFA_ROOT/bin/ofa`, then `bash -lic 'command -v ofa'`, then the Kestrel deploy default `/nopt/nrel/apps/cpu_stack/software/openfoam/assistant/bin/ofa`). Set explicitly on non-Kestrel installs or if your `module load assistant` is not sourced by an interactive login shell.

enumDescriptions: Do not set OFA_MODEL. bin/ofa falls back to its own default (currently gemma4:31b-it-q8_0) — same value this setting defaults to. Choose this if you want the extension to always track bin/ofa's default rather than pinning it here.
Google Gemma 4 — 31B, ~19 GB (Q4_K_M). In TESTED_MODELS. Same base weights as the Q8 default but lower fidelity; pick this if you need the VRAM for other things.

(default) Google Gemma 4 — 31B Q8_0 (~34 GB). In TESTED_MODELS. Higher precision than the Q4 variant above. Runs at the model's full 262144 context: only 10 of 60 layers use full attention, so the KV cache is just ~21 GiB at 256K. Same base weights as gemma4:31b.
Google Gemma 4 — 26B, smaller sibling of the default. Same sampling.
Meta Llama 4 Scout — 108B MoE. Long context (capped at 128K). Sampling: T=0.6, top_p=0.9.
Meta Llama 3.3 — 70B dense. No vision, no thinking. Sampling: T=0.6, top_p=0.9.

Microsoft phi-4 — 14B. Small + strong reasoning. NOTE: no tools capability upstream — combining with `ofa.enableTools=true` silently degrades to Ask-mode behavior (schema forwards, tool_calls never emitted).
IBM Granite 4 — 32B MoE (~19 GB active). Tools-capable. Sampling: T=0.7, top_p=0.95.
OpenAI gpt-oss — 116.8B MoE (~5B active), MXFP4, ~65 GB. Tools + thinking, no vision. Sourced from shared Kestrel install via symlink (no duplicate bytes). Sampling: T=1.0, top_p=1.0 per OpenAI card.

Meta Muse Glimmer — 30B (27.9B text + 1.92B vision projector), ~18 GB. Apache 2.0, agentic/tool-use tuned, vision + thinking capable. Sampling: T=1.0, top_p=0.95, top_k=64 per Ollama's published params.

NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning — 30B MoE (3B active), Q8_0 (~35 GB). Non-Chinese. Tools + thinking, NO vision. Hybrid Mamba-transformer: runs the FULL 1M-token context on one H100 (weights + KV = ~43 GB). Fast (~208 tok/s). Sampling: T=0.6, top_p=0.95, top_k=40. NOT yet in TESTED_MODELS — validate before relying on it.
ofa.model.markdownDescription: LLM backing `ofa --serve`. Passed to bin/ofa as `OFA_MODEL` at spawn. Default here (`gemma4:31b-it-q8_0`) matches bin/ofa's own CLI default; pick the empty option to explicitly inherit whatever bin/ofa's default is rather than pinning it. **Server-wide, not per-model-picker-entry**: all eight `OFA · *` entries in the Copilot Chat picker route to the SAME LLM selected here — they differ only in prompt + RAG. To change the LLM you must run **OFA: Disconnect** then **OFA: Connect** so a new `ofa --serve` process picks up the new value.

enumDescriptions: (default) Local inference on your allocated Kestrel GPU node via Ollama. Nothing leaves NLR.

Route model calls to an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM gateway (set ofa.litellm.baseUrl) for proprietary/frontier models, while still using ofa's LOCAL RAG. Set ofa.model to a gateway model id (e.g. gemini-3.7-flash). NOTE: your prompt + retrieved context are sent to the gateway (not local-only). The API KEY is NOT set here — ofa reads it on the node from $OFA_LITELLM_API_KEY or the 0600 file $OFA_SCRATCH/.ofa_litellm_key.
ofa.backend.markdownDescription: LLM backend for `ofa --serve`. `ollama` = local (default, nothing leaves NLR). `litellm` = route to an internal OpenAI-compatible gateway for proprietary models while keeping ofa's local RAG. Passed as `OFA_BACKEND`. When `litellm`, also set **`ofa.litellm.baseUrl`** and **`ofa.model`** (to a gateway model id). The API key is read on the compute node (never through VS Code): write it to `$OFA_SCRATCH/.ofa_litellm_key` (chmod 600) or export `OFA_LITELLM_API_KEY`. Run **OFA: Disconnect** then **OFA: Connect** after changing.

ofa.litellm.baseUrl.markdownDescription: LiteLLM gateway base URL, including `/v1` (e.g. `https://litellm.nlr.gov/v1`). Used only when `ofa.backend` is `litellm`. Passed as `OFA_LITELLM_BASE_URL`. The API key is intentionally NOT a setting — it is read on the node from `$OFA_LITELLM_API_KEY` or the 0600 file `$OFA_SCRATCH/.ofa_litellm_key`, so it never passes through VS Code.

ofa.litellmModel.markdownDescription: Gateway model id to use when `ofa.backend` is `litellm` (e.g. `gemini-3.7-flash`). Free-text because the available models are gateway-specific — see the LiteLLM web UI for the list. Passed as `OFA_MODEL`. Ignored in `ollama` mode (which uses the `ofa.model` dropdown instead). Run **OFA: Disconnect** then **OFA: Connect** after changing.

ofa.enableTools.markdownDescription: Pass `--serve-enable-tools` to `ofa --serve`. Enables tool-calling passthrough so VS Code Agent mode can chain file edits / terminal commands.

ofa.laptopSideBridgePort.markdownDescription: Login-node port for the `ssh -N -L` bridge that forwards `kestrel-login:PORT` → `<compute-node>:<remote-port>`. VS Code Remote-SSH auto-forwards this to `laptop:PORT`, so your laptop's `chatLanguageModels.json` can pin `http://localhost:PORT/v1/chat/completions` and stay valid across SLURM allocations. Match the port your existing `byok-update-config.py` setup used (default `49643`).

ofa.autoConnectOnStartup.markdownDescription: Automatically call `OFA: Connect` when a workspace opens on a detected Kestrel host. Opt-in because it burns a SLURM allocation whether you plan to use ofa or not.

ofa.healthProbeIntervalSeconds.markdownDescription: How often to poll `/healthz` on the ofa endpoint. First failed probe triggers the silent-reconnect flow.

ofa.silentReconnect.markdownDescription: When the SLURM job expires mid-session, silently re-allocate and rewire the endpoint (a toast notifies the user). Disable to be prompted before each re-allocate.

scripts.package: npm run build && npx --yes @vscode/vsce@^3 package --no-yarn --no-dependencies -o ofa-vscode.vsix
